editorial_candidates.source_claim: The Radon data are known for an open set of line normals Θ, and the Fourier-slice identity gives the Fourier transform on the corresponding open frequency sector; compact support then supplies analytic continuation to all frequencies.
editorial_candidates.why_warranted: A schematic can distinguish the measured normal arc and its frequency wedge from the global conclusion that follows by analytic continuation, helping readers keep the limited acquisition geometry separate from the uniqueness conclusion.
editorial_candidates.content_to_draw_or_check: In an explicitly schematic frequency-plane view, mark Θ as an open arc of unit normals on S¹; map each normal θ to the line ξ=σθ, σ∈R, showing the symmetric open wedge W_Θ where Fourier values are directly known from zero Radon data. Label the compact-support analytic-continuation step as extending vanishing from that open wedge to all ξ∈R², then the Fourier uniqueness conclusion f=0. Preserve the line-normal convention and avoid suggesting stability or a measured full-angle dataset.
editorial_candidates.limitation: Optional explanatory schematic only; the source proof already gives the Fourier-slice and analytic-continuation argument and does not depend on a figure.
